component.name: jira
component.title: Jira
component.description: Create, update and query issues in Atlassian Jira, and poll Jira for new issues, new comments and changed fields.
component.label: document

delay.description: The time between two polls of the consumer, in milliseconds unless the timeUnit option sets another unit. The producer does not use it.

jiraUrl.description: The URL of the Jira server, for example https://jira.example.com, to which the component sends its REST API requests.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

configuration.label: advanced
configuration.description: The shared configuration of the endpoints, as an org.apache.camel.component.jira.JiraConfiguration. Each endpoint starts from a copy of it, and the options of the endpoint override the copy.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

accessToken.label: security
accessToken.description: The access token. If none of the consumerKey, privateKey and verificationCode options is set, the component sends it as a personal access token in a Bearer Authorization header. Otherwise it is the OAuth 1.0a access token. Not used when the username option is set.

consumerKey.label: security
consumerKey.description: The consumer key of the OAuth 1.0a application link in Jira, for OAuth authentication with the privateKey, verificationCode and accessToken options. Not used when the username option is set.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for basic authentication, or an API token on Jira Cloud. Only used when the username option is set.

privateKey.label: security
privateKey.description: The RSA private key of the OAuth 1.0a consumer, as Base64-encoded PKCS#8 without the PEM header and footer. The component signs each request with it (RSA-SHA1), for OAuth authentication. Not used when the username option is set.

username.label: security
username.description: The username for basic authentication, which is the email address of the account on Jira Cloud. If set, the component uses basic authentication with the password option, and does not use the accessToken and OAuth options.

verificationCode.label: security
verificationCode.description: The OAuth 1.0a verification code (oauth_verifier) that Jira showed when the user authorized the request token, for OAuth authentication with the consumerKey, privateKey and accessToken options. Not used when the username option is set.

CamelJiraIssueAssigneeId.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueAssigneeId.description: The ID of the user to assign the issue to, which is the account ID on Jira Cloud, for addIssue and updateIssue. Not used when the CamelJiraIssueAssignee header is set.

CamelJiraIssueAssignee.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueAssignee.description: The username of the user to assign the issue to, for addIssue and updateIssue. Jira Cloud identifies users by account ID instead, so use the CamelJiraIssueAssigneeId header there.

CamelJiraIssueComponents.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueComponents.description: The comma-separated list of the names of the project components to set on the issue, for addIssue and updateIssue. For updateIssue, the list replaces the components of the issue.

CamelJiraIssueChanged.label: consumer
CamelJiraIssueChanged.description: The name of the watched field that changed, as written in the watchedFields option, for example Status. The watchUpdates consumer sets it.

CamelJiraIssueKey.description: The key of the issue, for example CAMEL-1234. Required by every producer type except addIssue and addIssueLink. The watchUpdates consumer sets it to the key of the changed issue.

CamelJiraIssuePriorityId.label: producer
CamelJiraIssuePriorityId.description: The ID of the priority of the issue, for addIssue and updateIssue. If not set, the producer looks up the ID of the priority that the CamelJiraIssuePriorityName header names.

CamelJiraIssuePriorityName.label: producer
CamelJiraIssuePriorityName.description: The name of the priority of the issue, for example High, for addIssue and updateIssue. Only used when the CamelJiraIssuePriorityId header is not set, and the name must match exactly.

CamelJiraIssueProjectKey.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueProjectKey.description: The key of the project to create the issue in, for example CAMEL. Required for addIssue.

CamelJiraIssueSummary.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueSummary.description: The summary of the issue. Required for addIssue. For updateIssue, it replaces the summary of the issue.

CamelJiraIssueTransitionId.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueTransitionId.description: The ID of the workflow transition to perform on the issue, for transitionIssue, which requires it. Jira lists the transitions of an issue at /rest/api/2/issue/{issueIdOrKey}/transitions.

CamelJiraIssueTypeId.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueTypeId.description: The ID of the issue type, for addIssue and updateIssue. If not set, the producer looks up the ID of the issue type that the CamelJiraIssueTypeName header names. addIssue requires one of the two headers.

CamelJiraIssueTypeName.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueTypeName.description: The name of the issue type, for example Bug, for addIssue and updateIssue. Only used when the CamelJiraIssueTypeId header is not set, and the name must match exactly.

CamelJiraIssueWatchedIssues.label: consumer
CamelJiraIssueWatchedIssues.description: The comma-separated list of the keys of the issues that the watchUpdates consumer watches. The consumer builds the list when it starts, and again when the number of issues that the JQL query returns changes.

CamelJiraIssueWatchersAdd.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueWatchersAdd.description: The comma-separated list of the usernames, or of the account IDs on Jira Cloud, of the users to add as watchers of the issue, for addIssue and watchers.

CamelJiraIssueWatchersRemove.label: producer
CamelJiraIssueWatchersRemove.description: The comma-separated list of the usernames of the users to remove as watchers of the issue, for watchers.

CamelJiraParentIssueKey.label: producer
CamelJiraParentIssueKey.description: The key of the first issue of the link, which the producer sends as the inward issue. Required for addIssueLink.

CamelJiraChildIssueKey.label: producer
CamelJiraChildIssueKey.description: The key of the second issue of the link, which the producer sends as the outward issue. Required for addIssueLink.

CamelJiraLinkType.label: producer
CamelJiraLinkType.description: The name of the issue link type, for example Blocks or Duplicate. Required for addIssueLink.

CamelJiraMinutesSpent.label: producer
CamelJiraMinutesSpent.description: The time spent on the issue in minutes, for the work log that addWorkLog adds, which requires it.

consumerOut.description: One message per new Issue (newIssues) or new Comment (newComments). watchUpdates sends one per watched field that changed, with its new value, such as the Status or the BasicPriority (null when cleared), or the Issue with sendOnlyUpdatedField=false

producerIn.description: Read as text: the description for addIssue and updateIssue, the comment for addComment and addWorkLog, which fail without a body, and an optional comment for transitionIssue and addIssueLink; a Map or a POJO is sent as its toString(), so marshal it first. attach uploads a file, or text, bytes or a stream named by the CamelFileName header. The other types read only headers

producerOut.description: The Issue created for addIssue, the Issue for fetchIssue and the List of its Comments for fetchComments. The other types leave the body unchanged

type.description: The operation of the endpoint, case-insensitive. The consumer types are newIssues, newComments and watchUpdates. The producer types are addIssue, addComment, addIssueLink, addWorkLog, attach, deleteIssue, fetchComments, fetchIssue, transitionIssue, updateIssue and watchers.

delay.description: The time between two polls of the consumer, in milliseconds unless the timeUnit option sets another unit. The producer does not use it.

jiraUrl.description: The URL of the Jira server, for example https://jira.example.com, to which the component sends its REST API requests.

jql.label: consumer
jql.description: The JQL query that selects the issues that the consumer reads, for example project=CAMEL AND status=Open. The newIssues consumer adds a condition on the creation date and ORDER BY created DESC to it, so the query must not have an ORDER BY clause. Wrap the query in RAW() so that Camel does not decode it, for example RAW(project in (MYP, COM) AND resolution = Unresolved).

maxResults.label: consumer
maxResults.description: The maximum number of issues that the consumer reads from the JQL search in one poll, or no limit if 0 or less: newComments reads the comments of these issues, and watchUpdates watches them. The newIssues consumer reads every issue created since its previous poll and uses this value as the page size of the search, at most 50.

sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.label: consumer
sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

sendOnlyUpdatedField.label: consumer
sendOnlyUpdatedField.description: Whether the watchUpdates consumer sends only the new value of the changed field as the body, for example a Status, or null when the field was cleared. If false, the body is the whole updated Issue. Either way, the consumer sends one message per watched field that changed.

watchedFields.label: consumer
watchedFields.description: The comma-separated list of the issue fields that the watchUpdates consumer watches for changes, without spaces. Each name is the name of a getter of com.atlassian.jira.rest.client.api.domain.Issue without the get prefix, case-sensitive, for example Status, Priority, Summary or Assignee.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

pollStrategy.label: consumer,advanced
pollStrategy.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

backoffErrorThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffErrorThreshold.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffIdleThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffIdleThreshold.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffMultiplier.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffMultiplier.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

greedy.label: consumer,scheduler
greedy.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

healthCheckMaxPollDuration.label: consumer,scheduler
healthCheckMaxPollDuration.description: How long a poll may run before the health check of the consumer reports DOWN. The health check is otherwise based on the polls that are done, so it stays UP while a poll hangs, for example on a read without timeout from a connection that went silent. A poll includes routing the messages it polled, so set this above the longest poll you expect. The poll is not interrupted. The value is in millis (not affected by timeUnit). The default 0 turns this off.

initialDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
initialDelay.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

repeatCount.label: consumer,scheduler
repeatCount.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

runLoggingLevel.label: consumer,scheduler
runLoggingLevel.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

scheduledExecutorService.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduledExecutorService.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

scheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduler.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

schedulerProperties.label: consumer,scheduler
schedulerProperties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

startScheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
startScheduler.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

timeUnit.label: consumer,scheduler
timeUnit.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

useFixedDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
useFixedDelay.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.

accessToken.label: security
accessToken.description: The access token. If none of the consumerKey, privateKey and verificationCode options is set, the component sends it as a personal access token in a Bearer Authorization header. Otherwise it is the OAuth 1.0a access token. Not used when the username option is set.

consumerKey.label: security
consumerKey.description: The consumer key of the OAuth 1.0a application link in Jira, for OAuth authentication with the privateKey, verificationCode and accessToken options. Not used when the username option is set.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for basic authentication, or an API token on Jira Cloud. Only used when the username option is set.

privateKey.label: security
privateKey.description: The RSA private key of the OAuth 1.0a consumer, as Base64-encoded PKCS#8 without the PEM header and footer. The component signs each request with it (RSA-SHA1), for OAuth authentication. Not used when the username option is set.

username.label: security
username.description: The username for basic authentication, which is the email address of the account on Jira Cloud. If set, the component uses basic authentication with the password option, and does not use the accessToken and OAuth options.

verificationCode.label: security
verificationCode.description: The OAuth 1.0a verification code (oauth_verifier) that Jira showed when the user authorized the request token, for OAuth authentication with the consumerKey, privateKey and accessToken options. Not used when the username option is set.
